🫀 Webcam Heart Rate Monitor

Version: 1.0 | Status: Production Ready

Quick Navigation:
Product Requirements Architecture Signal Pipeline API Reference Limitations

1. Product Summary

Build a privacy-first webpage that uses a computer webcam to estimate a user's heart rate without physical contact via remote photoplethysmography (rPPG).

Core Features

  • Live webcam feed with face-position guidance
  • Real-time rPPG analysis from facial color changes
  • Heart rate display in beats per minute (BPM)
  • Live pulse waveform and HR trend graphs
  • Signal confidence indicator (Good/Fair/Poor)
  • 10-second calibration minimum before displaying BPM
  • Session summary with min/max/avg statistics
  • Explicit medical disclaimer and privacy notice

2. User Experience Flow

Step Duration User Action Display
Introduction Instant Read privacy notice, click "Start" Welcome screen, disclaimer, educational info
Camera Setup 1-2s Grant camera permission Mirrored webcam preview, face guide oval, positioning hints
Calibration 10s Sit still, face centered, even lighting Progress bar, "Finding your pulse…", signal quality indicator
Measurement 30–60s Remain still Large BPM, confidence badge, live pulse waveform, HR trend
Results Instant Review or "Measure Again" Average BPM, min/max range, signal quality %, summary graph

3. Functional Requirements

Camera

  • Use navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()
  • Request video only (no audio)
  • Target 640×480 or 1280×720 at ~30 FPS
  • Chrome/Edge desktop; localhost/HTTPS only

Face & Skin Detection

  • Use MediaPipe Face Landmarker to locate face
  • Extract RGB samples from: forehead, left cheek, right cheek
  • Avoid: eyes, eyebrows, mouth, hair, background
  • Track regions as face moves

Heart Rate Estimation

  • Capture RGB intensity from face regions each frame
  • Apply POS (Plane-Orthogonal-to-Skin) algorithm
  • Remove slow lighting trends (detrending)
  • Apply frequency range 0.7–3.0 Hz (42–180 BPM)
  • Analyze 10–15 second rolling window
  • Identify dominant pulse frequency via FFT
  • Smooth BPM using exponential moving average
  • CRITICAL: Hide BPM when confidence < 60%

Signal Quality Scoring

  • Illumination: Brightness level consistency
  • Motion: Frame-to-frame RGB stability
  • Continuity: Frames captured vs. expected
  • Spectral Peak: Strength of detected frequency
  • Result: Confidence = (ill + motion + cont + peak) / 4 × face_confidence
Guard Rail: The most important guardrail is to withhold the BPM number when confidence is poor. Transparent signal quality over impressive-looking but unreliable numbers.

Stack

  • Privacy: All processing local; no API calls
  • Transparency: Multiple disclaimers visible at each step

5. Signal Processing Pipeline

Frame Capture (30 FPS)
      ↓
Face Detection (MediaPipe)
      ↓
Extract RGB from Skin Regions (Forehead + Cheeks)
      ↓
Maintain Rolling Buffer (300 frames ≈ 10s)
      ↓
Apply POS Algorithm (R-G, G-B decomposition)
      ↓
Normalize & Detrend (remove lighting trends)
      ↓
Compute FFT on Signal
      ↓
Find Peak Frequency in 0.7-3.0 Hz Range
      ↓
Convert Frequency → BPM
      ↓
Calculate Confidence Score
      ↓
IF confidence ≥ 0.6 AND elapsed ≥ 10s:
  Display BPM + Confidence Badge
ELSE:
  Show "Waiting for stable signal…"
      ↓
Update Live Charts
      ↓
Loop at next frame

Algorithm Details

POS (Plane-Orthogonal-to-Skin)

L1 = R - G
L2 = G - B
S1 = normalize(L1)
S2 = normalize(L2)
P = S1 - S2 × (std(L1) / std(L2))
pulse = detrend(normalize(P))

FFT Frequency Detection

fft = DFT(pulse_signal)
magnitudes = |fft_bins|
peak_bin = argmax(magnitudes)
peak_hz = (peak_bin × sampling_rate) / window_length
bpm = round(peak_hz × 60)
confidence = peak_magnitude / sqrt(window_length)

Confidence Scoring

illumination = assess brightness level (0–1)
motion = assess RGB frame-to-frame stability (0–1)
continuity = frames_captured / frames_expected (0–1)
spectral_peak = min(1, peak_magnitude / 100) (0–1)
score = (illumination + motion + continuity + spectral_peak) / 4 × face_confidence
final = max(0, min(1, score))

6. Core Function API

Signal Processing

Function Input Output Purpose
estimateBPM(frames, previousBPM) RGBFrame[] BPMEstimate | null Compute BPM from frame history
posAlgorithm(r, g, b) number[] number[] Extract pulse signal
computeFFT(signal) number[] FFTResult Find dominant frequency
calculateSignalQuality(...) RGBFrame[], DetectedFace, magnitude SignalQuality Score signal reliability
normalize(signal) number[] number[] Z-score normalization
detrend(signal) number[] number[] Remove linear trend

Face Detection

Function Purpose Returns
initFaceLandmarker() Initialize MediaPipe async Promise<void>
detectFace(video) Find face in video frame DetectedFace | null
getSkinRegions(face) Extract forehead + cheeks ROI Region[]

Camera

Function Purpose
captureFrame(video) Get ImageData from video
captureFrameRGB(video, regions) Average RGB from regions → RGBFrame
useCamera() React hook for camera stream

7. TypeScript Type Definitions

interface RGBFrame {
  timestamp: number       // milliseconds
  r: number             // 0–255
  g: number             // 0–255
  b: number             // 0–255
}

interface BPMEstimate {
  bpm: number           // beats per minute
  confidence: number    // 0–1 (only display if ≥ 0.6)
  timestamp: number
}

interface SignalQuality {
  score: number         // 0–1
  illumination: number  // 0–1
  motion: number        // 0–1
  spectralPeak: number  // 0–1
  continuity: number    // 0–1
  reason?: string       // diagnostic message
}

interface DetectedFace {
  x: number
  y: number
  width: number
  height: number
  confidence: number    // 0–1
  landmarks: Array<{x, y}>
}

interface SessionSummary {
  averageBPM: number
  minBPM: number
  maxBPM: number
  goodSignalPercent: number
  duration: number
}

8. Known Limitations & Error Handling

Measurement Limitations

  • Lighting: Requires even, bright lighting (avoid shadows, backlight, dim)
  • Stillness: Movement, talking, chewing degrades signal
  • Accuracy: ±5 BPM typical under ideal conditions
  • Not Medical: Experimental tool; not for diagnostics
  • Single Face: Fails with multiple faces; requires exactly one
  • Frontal Only: Side profiles not detected

Error States (Handled Explicitly)

  • Camera permission denied → "Camera access denied"
  • No camera available → "No camera found"
  • Browser unsupported → "WebRTC not supported"
  • Face not detected → Dashed guide box, "Position your face here"
  • Multiple faces → "Please show only one face"
  • Insufficient lighting → Signal quality: Poor
  • Excessive movement → Signal quality: Poor
  • Weak spectral peak → Withhold BPM until stable
  • Tab backgrounded → Pause measurement
  • Camera disconnected → Show error, allow retry
Safety Guarantee: Never display an unreliable BPM number. BPM is only shown when:
  1. Confidence score ≥ 0.6
  2. Measurement duration ≥ 10 seconds
  3. Face continuously detected

9. Privacy & Deployment

Privacy Guarantee

  • ✅ No uploads: Video never leaves browser
  • ✅ No recording: Frames not saved to disk
  • ✅ No analytics: No tracking of measurements
  • ✅ Session-only: Results in localStorage, cleared on tab close
  • ✅ Open source: Full code available for inspection
